data.description:
## Summary

The blue-green deploy swaps the nginx `/mcp` upstream to the new container the moment it is
healthy. MCP streamable-HTTP sessions are STATEFUL and STICKY to the container that created
them, so every client holding an `Mcp-Session-Id` is instantly orphaned: its next request is
routed to a container that has never heard of that session and answers **404 Session expired**.
The client surfaces it as an opaque transport error, not as a reconnect signal.

Because autodeploy ticks every 2 minutes, ANY merge touching `MCP_PATHS` kills every live agent
session on the box.

## Observed (GitHub Copilot CLI, same host)

Every tool call failed after the session had been working:

    ✗ fsck            MCP server 'rebar': Error: MCP request failed: Transport send error:
                      Transport [rmcp::transport::worker::WorkerT...
    ✗ grounding_info  ... same
    ✗ validate / show_ticket / audit_trail / summary / list_tickets  ... same

The client's own reasoning: 'All the subsequent calls now fail with "Session expired (HTTP 404)"
— a different error than the transport issue seen before.'

**The session was demonstrably WORKING first.** The earlier `unreal-milky-sloth` BigInt failure
is the proof: a serialization error means the server RETURNED a payload the client then failed to
serialize. Transport was healthy. This is a functional -> dead transition, not a never-worked.

## Root cause — confirmed from the box, with timing

Landing Gerrit 2271 (an `MCP_PATHS` change) triggered an mcp redeploy:

    18:51:04Z  change 2271 submitted / merged
    18:54:09Z  autodeploy begins rebuilding the mcp image
    18:54:24Z  image built
    18:54:29Z  "mcp cutover complete: /mcp upstream now 127.0.0.1:8093
                (deploy DONE; not waiting on in-flight drain)"
    18:54:29Z  "mcp retire: 'docker stop --time 1260' rebar-mcp-9966198879a2-8092 in background
                (graceful SIGTERM self-drain; never rm -f a serving container)"
    18:54:31Z  "mcp redeployed + healthy at 127.0.0.1:8093"

The upstream moved 8092 -> 8093 at 18:54:29. Sessions created on 8092 could only ever be served
by 8092.

**The graceful-drain design does not help, and its logs imply protection it cannot provide.**
Retiring the old container with `docker stop --time 1260` (21 minutes) keeps it ALIVE, but the
nginx upstream has ALREADY been switched, so no further client request is routed to it. The long
grace period drains nothing for session continuity: what needed preserving was the ROUTE to the
session's own container, not the container's lifetime. `not waiting on in-flight drain` is
accurate and the retire message reads reassuringly, but together they describe a drain that
cannot apply to sticky sessions.

## Secondary observation (may warrant its own ticket)

The retired container did NOT stop. `rebar-mcp-9966198879a2-8092` is still `Up 2 hours
(unhealthy)` and the retire line repeats at 18:55:20 and 18:57:33 — autodeploy re-issues the
retire on later ticks. Two containers are bound to 8092/8093 while one is wedged unhealthy.

## Impact

Any agent session using the MCP server dies without warning on any mcp deploy, mid-task, with an
error that names a Rust transport internal (`rmcp::transport::worker::WorkerT...`) rather than
telling the operator to reconnect. This directly undermines the AGENTS.md mandate to route
tracker operations through MCP: the mandated path is unreliable by construction on a box that
redeploys every 2 minutes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A client session survives an mcp blue-green cutover, OR the client receives an explicit,
      actionable session-expired signal it can act on (reconnect) rather than an opaque
      transport error.
- [ ] The retire path either preserves routing to the old container for the life of its existing
      sessions, or the logs stop describing a graceful drain that cannot protect sticky sessions.
- [ ] A retired container actually terminates; `docker ps` does not accumulate wedged unhealthy
      containers, and the retire is not re-issued every tick.
- [ ] Regression coverage asserts the chosen behaviour (session survival or a clean expiry
      signal) across a simulated cutover.

## How it was found

Reported by an operator from a live Copilot CLI session; root-caused against the box's autodeploy
journal. Discovered while working `unreal-milky-sloth`, whose BigInt error is what establishes
the session was healthy beforehand.
data.title: MCP blue-green cutover destroys every live client session: upstream swaps mid-session, clients get opaque transport errors
